## Root cause

The DOM client applies **all properties before creating a node's children** (`emitNode` at `lib/java/pathland-view-core/.../Emitter.kt:797-813`, `emitSubtreeInto` at `:992-1020`). When `ViewThatFits` swaps to a freshly-emitted candidate, the new `<button>` receives `PROP_LABEL` before its `<svg>` icon exists.

In `lib/typescript/src/apply.ts:1339-1381` (`applyStringProperty`), `PROP_LABEL` and `PROP_TEXT` share a case. With no icon child yet:

- it sets `aria-label="Play"` on the button (`:1367-1372`), then
- falls through to `setNodeText(el, text)` (`:1377-1379`), and `setNodeText` writes `textContent` because the button still has **zero** element children (`:1318-1320`).

Then the icon is inserted → `Play<svg…>`. SSR is correct because it renders the finished tree, not deltas.

Also, the icon lookup at `:1346-1348` uses `el.querySelector("svg.pathland-icon")`, so a later label update would move the accessible name from the button onto its decorative icon — divergent from SSR (`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs:909-924`).

## Plan

1. **Fix `applyStringProperty` in `lib/typescript/src/apply.ts`**
   - Treat only the element itself as an icon (`el.matches("svg.pathland-icon")`), never a descendant icon.
   - Split the shared case:
     - `PROP_LABEL` = accessible name only: media `alt`; self-icon `syncIconAria`; slider inner-input `aria-label`; `.pathland-label` span text; otherwise `aria-label` on the element. **Never** call `setNodeText`.
     - `PROP_TEXT` = visible text (keep `setNodeText`/`.pathland-label` behavior).
   - Remove/refresh the stale "caption" comments.

2. **Regression tests in `lib/typescript/test/apply.test.ts`**
   - LABEL emitted on a freshly created button *before* its icon child is inserted: button has no text node, `aria-label="Play"` on the button, icon stays `aria-hidden`.
   - A subsequent LABEL update after the icon exists keeps `aria-label` on the button (not the svg) and injects no text.
   - Existing tests stay green: composite-children preservation (`:828`), icon self-label (`:1414`), slider inner input (`:854`).

3. **Update `lib/typescript/status.md`**
   - Document that LABEL mirrors SSR: accessible name only (ICON/IMAGE/SLIDER/TEXT_FIELD special-cased; controls/composites get `aria-label`; never visible text).

4. **Rebuild + sync the shipped bundle**
   - `cd lib/typescript && npm test && npm run typecheck`
   - `npm run build:all` — regenerates `dist/`, copies the hashed bundle + `dom-renderer.current` into `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/` and `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/resources/static/_pathland/`, pruning the stale `dom-renderer-d14b432bd728.js`.

5. **Verify end-to-end**
   - Rebuild/run the Spring or Quarkus demo and resize across the 200px fit threshold; confirm the swapped play button contains only the `<svg>` and keeps `aria-label` with no `Play` text node.

Rejected alternative: reordering the emitter to emit children before properties. It is a protocol-wide change affecting golden traces/renderers and still leaves the resync re-apply path broken; the DOM renderer should mirror SSR semantics regardless of delta order.

    private fun mount(snapshot: Boolean = false): Mounted {

        )
        return Mounted(result, sink, store)
    }

        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "The Pathland Dream"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "The Foundation"))
        assertFalse(anySetText(frame, "Now Playing"))

        assertTrue(anySetText(wide, "Up Next"))
        assertEquals(0, countCreate(wide, Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER))

        assertTrue(anySetText(withSidebar, "Now Playing"))

    }

        controller.register()

        controller.playing(playing)
        controller.position(seekRequest)
        controller.volume(volumeRequest)
        controller.time(position)
        controller.volumeReport(volume)
        controller.onEnded { ended() }

## Implemented

- **`MusicPlayerView`** — Apple Music-style root: one root `SizeThatFits`
  selects narrow (no volume), medium (volume), or wide (volume + `NowPlayingSidebar`),
  with the floating `PlayerBar`.
- **Persisted player state** — owned by `MediaPlayerService` (`player.position`, `player.playing`,
  `player.track`, `player.volume`, `player.seekRequest`, `player.volumeRequest`)
  and created with `Signals.state` while the framework's session state is active.
- **App-driven media** — `MediaPlayerService` owns and registers the
  `MediaController`, and the emitter projects it as a pinned root node; every fit
  candidate shares the same controller. `MEDIA_*` reports feed position/volume
  and `MEDIA_ENDED` advances the track.
- **Seek/volume decoupling** — `SeekControl` buffers drags and commits on release;
  `PercentSeek` maps seconds to 0..100; `VolumeControl` separates report from
  command (each in its own file under `player/controls/`).
- **Lyrics** — synchronized two-line karaoke pill driven by the parsed SRT cues.
- **Window metadata** — track-derived title/description and `locale("en")`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — optional `adUrl` appends a `ProxyView` in the sidebar.
- **`AdView`** — the small sponsored-proxy origin app: a title, a button, and a

## Diagnosis

Both failures come from the uncommitted `TransportControls.kt` change (introducing a **nested** `ViewThatFits`), not from the TypeScript fix.

1. **`MusicPlayerViewTest.libraryRendersTracksAndAlbumArt:81`**
   `assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, SIZE_THAT_FITS))` now gets **2** — the root layout fit plus the new transport fit. This assertion was set to `1` by commit `c9173833` precisely when the nested fit was removed, so it's stale for the new feature.

2. **`MusicPlayerFitMediaTest.transportStillWorksAfterAFitCrossing:188`**
   The test's `lastLabelId(frames, "Play")` picks the **last** `LABEL=Play` ever emitted. With the nested fit, the initial snapshot emits a play button in both nested candidates per root candidate. The last one (wide nested candidate) is **deleted** when the nested slot downgrades during the `2→0` root crossing, so `pointerUp` targets a dead id and no `PLAYBACK_STATE=1` is emitted. The surviving/attached play button still has its tap action; the helper just selects the wrong node.

   Verified by tracing `reconcileSnapshotFit` (`Emitter.kt:246-314`) + `reconcileNode`/`reconcileChildren`: after `accept(2), accept(0), accept(2)` only the nested *compact* play button remains registered in `result.tapActions()`.

## Plan (keep the nested transport fit)

1. **`MusicPlayerViewTest.kt`**
   - Update line 81 to `assertEquals(2, countCreate(frame, Components.SIZE_THAT_FITS))` with a comment: root layout fit + transport compact/full fit.
   - All other fit assertions (`0` creates after a root swap, snapshot child count = 3, slider counts) remain valid; no other changes.

2. **`MusicPlayerFitMediaTest.kt`**
   - Make the play-button lookup attachment-aware: choose the last `LABEL="Play"` node whose id is still in `mounted.result.tapActions()` (the render result maps are live views of the current routing tables), instead of the last label ever emitted.
   - Keep the existing assertion that the tap produces `PLAYBACK_STATE=1` on the pinned controller; optionally add `assertTrue(result.tapActions().containsKey(playId))` for clarity.

3. **Docs/comment hygiene**
   - `MusicPlayerView.kt:61-64`: the comment saying the root breakpoint "avoids a nested fit slot" is now false. Reword: the *volume/sidebar* breakpoint stays at the root; the transport's compact/full switch is a nested `SizeThatFits` driven by `FIT_CHANGED`.
   - `lib/java/pathland-demo-views-kotlin/status.md`: change "one root `SizeThatFits`" to mention the root fit plus the transport's nested compact/full fit.

4. **Verify**
   - `cd lib/java && mvn -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin -am test` (or the original full build) — all tests green.
   - Re-run `lib/typescript` tests are already green; no further TS changes needed.

### Alternative (if you'd rather not keep a nested fit)

Remove the nested `ViewThatFits` from `TransportControls` and drive the compact/full transport from the existing root candidates (e.g. a `showBackForward` flag per root candidate). That restores the "one root fit" invariant from `c9173833` and requires no emitter/test-helper changes, but loses the transport's independent 200px breakpoint.

I recommend the first plan (keep the feature, fix the stale count and the attached-button lookup). Want me to proceed with that?
